title: SpotServe: Serving Generative Large Language Models on Preemptible Instances
problem: Large language model inference serving requires expensive GPU resources, making deployment costly at scale. Preemptible cloud instances offer much cheaper GPU access but can be terminated unexpectedly, challenging transparent service continuity.
motivation: Reducing monetary costs for LLM serving by harnessing cheaper preemptible resources could make AI services more economically viable and accessible.
method: SpotServe serves LLMs on preemptible GPU instances while handling preemptions through instance migration and state management. The system coordinates migration of inference workloads across instances when preemption occurs, maintaining service availability despite interruptions and managing memory-intensive model states.
key_novelty: Enables practical LLM inference serving on preemptible cloud instances by combining live migration strategies with state preservation to transparently tolerate frequent preemptions.
contributions: System architecture for transparently serving LLMs across preemptible instances
Preemption handling mechanisms including migration and state checkpointing
Cost-optimization strategies that leverage spot/preemptible resources
Empirical demonstration of significant cost savings for LLM inference workloads
limitations: Paper abstract does not discuss limitations or failure scenarios.
primary_theme: Cost-efficient LLM serving on preemptible cloud instances
